item.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation Cast Get Emotional In Last Recording Sessions

description.p: End of an era.When Final Fantasy VII Revelation launches on 8th April 2027, it will mark the conclusion of Square Enix's ambitious remake project that was first announced at E3 in 2015 – until its DLC expansions release, that is.So for the voice actors who have been bringing such iconic characters to life for so long, it's naturally going to be a pretty emotional time. In a video shared by Kenneth Shepard from Kotaku during a New York City Comic Con panel, we can see the cast partake in their final recording sessions for the game.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Wake Up, Samurai! Cyberpunk 2077 Is Getting A Live-Action Movie

description.p: But who will play Johnny Silverhand?Cyberpunk 2077 didn't get off to the best start when it originally launched in 2020, but it's now considered a success story. Since then, CD Projekt Red has polished it up, rolled out an animated Netflix series, and released a Switch 2 version of the title.A second game is also in development, and now, to add to all of this, a live-action movie set in the "Cyberpunk 2077" video game universe is in the works. According to the latest report, it's being done by Paramount Pictures, and "Transformers" movie producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura is working alongside CDPR on the film.Read the full article on nintendolife.com

item.title: Preview: 'Muramasa: Revenant Blades' Polishes Vanillaware's Gem To Shine Brighter Than Ever

description.p: Reforged.Muramasa: The Demon Blade originally launched on the Wii back in 2009, a title that we called "gorgeous, engrossing," and even underrated. We’ve been hoping to see a modern port of this gem for a long time now, and Vanillaware has delivered, with Muramasa: Revenant Blades coming to both Switch 1 and 2 in February next year.The PS Vita received Muramasa Rebirth in 2013, bringing updated music and localisation, followed by the Genroku Legends DLC, which added four new playable stories in addition to the original two. Revenant Blades combines Rebirth and Genroku Legends, meaning all six stories are available from launch. Think of this as a 'complete edition', then, finally accessible on current platforms.Read the full article on nintendolife.com
